newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico protests to U.S. over leaked allegations.
newsitem.headline: Mexico protests to U.S. over leaked allegations.

text.p: Mexico said on Wednesday it had protested to the United States over leaked allegations in the case of a former Mexican deputy attorney general accused of taking money from drug traffickers.
"The Foreign Ministry ... has asked that if such testimony and official documents exist, they be made known to the Mexican government," the ministry said in a statement.
"Mexico rejects efforts to harm the prestige of institutions based on illegal leaks of testimony not corroborated or proven in any court," it added.

The move followed publication in Mexico last weekend of documents that linked former prosecutor Mario Ruiz Massieu, former Mexican President Carlos Salinas de Gortari, his brother Raul and other officials to drug traffickers.
The Salinas brothers have denied the allegations and threatened legal action.

On Tuesday, U.S. District Judge Nancy Atlas ruled that until Ruiz Massieu comes to trial on March 10, lawyers from both sides in the case would not be allowed copies of sensitive information gathered during the pre-trial discovery process in order to avoid leaks.
The trial is a civil proceeding in which the U.S. government is trying to confiscate more than $9 million from his Houston bank account on grounds that it came from drug-related bribes.
The prosecution has said the release of the information had put the government's witnesses in danger and that one of the witnesses now did not wish to proceed.
The trial is part of a series of interlocking scandals in Mexico involving political murders and allegations of drug corruption.

Ruiz Massieu was assigned by then-president Salinas in September 1994 to investigate the murder of his brother, Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, who was a top leader of the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).
Francisco Ruiz Massieu was another of the officials implicated in the leaks, as was assassinated PRI presidential candidate Luis Donaldo Colosio.
Mario Ruiz Massieu stunned the country by resigning his post and blaming antidemocratic old-guard PRI politicians for blocking the probe.
But authorities then charged him with drug-related corruption in his previous job as chief of the anti-narcotics programme, and he fled Mexico only to be arrested in the United States.
In its diplomatic note, Mexico reiterated its wish to cooperate with the United States in fighting drug-trafficking.
